You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Nasdaq Hits Another Record; Apple Briefly Tops $5 Trillion; Sandisk Jumps 6.81% (September 23, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
US flash PMIs arrive tonight as higher-for-longer rates remain the central theme
The September S&P Global US manufacturing and services flash PMIs are scheduled for 21:45 Beijing time. Consensus estimates are approximately 53.6 for manufacturing and 55.8 for services.
Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michael Barr is scheduled to speak at 22:05 Beijing time. Markets will monitor his comments on inflation, financial conditions and the future rate path.
Following the Federal Reserve’s recent rate increase, officials continue to emphasize inflation control. Energy prices and resilient demand could limit the scope for an early policy shift.
Market Impact : Continued economic expansion could reinforce expectations that interest rates will remain elevated, pressuring valuations for technology stocks and crypto assets. A material slowdown in services activity would help ease the risk of another rise in Treasury yields.
International Commodities
Saudi Arabia restarts its East-West pipeline as supply expectations weigh on oil
Saudi Arabia has restarted its East-West oil pipeline at a reduced operating rate. The route carries crude to the Red Sea and allows exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
The pipeline has a design capacity of approximately 7 million barrels per day, although full repairs to damaged facilities could take six to eight weeks.
Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States reduces military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports, further easing some supply concerns.
Market Impact : Expectations of improving supply are keeping WTI near $90 per barrel and Brent near $99. The retreat from recent highs could reduce inflation expectations and support technology valuations, although unresolved Middle East risks are likely to keep energy-market volatility elevated.
International Economic Policy
Trump-Xi summit approaches with the trade truce and AI policy in focus
US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to meet in Washington on September 24.
The expected agenda includes extending the trade truce due to expire in November, agricultural and aircraft purchases, rare-earth supplies, advanced-technology restrictions and AI risk management.
Iran and Taiwan may also be discussed, but markets are primarily focused on whether the meeting produces a framework for more stable economic relations.
Market Impact : An extension of the trade truce could benefit semiconductors, cloud computing, consumer electronics and cross-border commerce. Signals of tighter technology restrictions would raise the risk premium across the AI supply chain.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Gold futures : Approximately $4,395.95 per ounce, up 0.45%.
Silver futures : Approximately $67.92 per ounce, up 2.09%.
WTI crude oil futures : Approximately $90.00 per barrel, down 0.57%.

US 10-year Treasury yield : Approximately 4.96%.
Driver Analysis : Expectations of improving Middle East supply are limiting crude’s upside, although geopolitical risks continue to support a premium in Brent. Gold is receiving support from safe-haven demand, while high interest rates and a firm dollar remain constraints. Silver is outperforming gold as precious-metal demand combines with stronger industrial-demand expectations.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approximately 86,443 USDT, up 0.64% over 24 hours, with approximately $40.07 billion in trading volume.
ETH : Approximately 2,760 USDT, up 0.21% over 24 hours, with approximately $15.24 billion in trading volume.

Total 24-hour market volume : Approximately $113.0 billion, down around 23% from the previous day.
Price, Volume & Large-Buyer Activity : BTC and ETH remain higher, while total market volume has declined materially, indicating less aggressive follow-through buying and consolidation near recent highs. The latest weekly disclosures show that Strategy purchased 950 BTC for approximately $75.7 million between September 14 and 20. BitMine acquired 27,562 ETH during the same reporting week, lifting its holdings to 5,983,940 ETH. These are the latest disclosed weekly purchases, not new intraday buying on September 23.
Driver Analysis : Bitcoin remains near an eight-month high, supported by institutional purchases and crypto ETF inflows, although the $90,000 area could become the next psychological resistance level. ETH continues to benefit from corporate treasury demand, staking income and asset-tokenization themes, but its 24-hour gain is currently smaller than Bitcoin’s.
